chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Movie stars and rising musicians on the scene
summary: Film stars like Sonny Tufts, Ava Gardner and Orson Welles came to the clubs, along with young musicians who became famous.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And during this period there was a lot of the movie stars frequenting the Jazz scene, like the after-hour places. The Streets of Paris, Sonny Tufts, he was popular at the time. He was one of our big patrons. You know, he'd show up. And when we'd go on to other places, guys like Torin(?) Bey, and Ava Gardner and her gang, and Herb Jeffries -- all kind of different stars would show up on the scene.

Orson Welles, sure. Ginger Rogers. C.P. Johnson was real popular at the time, that played the Latin drums, and he was doing a lot of work in the movies out there, and he would bring a lot of people out. Do you remember C.P. Johnson, played the congas in some of those early movies from Warner Brothers.
A lot of famous people would come over to hear the Jazz, you know. Like, I remember a lot of the big-name musicians, who became big names later, used to be on the avenue every night, you know.

Like Neal Hefti, Johnny Mandel... I could go on and name a whole lot of guys who used to be around. Art Pepper. So many guys used to be around on the scene. Russ Freeman used to be through there. Shelly Manne. Different guys would be down there. We'd all be getting together ganging up on the music, you know.
